title: timezone-aware-shift-annotator-and-compact-rotations-export
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a timezone-aware on-call shift annotator and a compact rotations exporter (CSV/ICS). Feature gated, opt-in via tzShiftAnnotator flag; no breaking changes to existing rotation storage or APIs.
body:
Motivation: Teams operating across multiple time zones (and frequent DST transitions) receive ambiguous on-call snippets in dashboards and pager messages. This makes handoffs error-prone and increases cognitive load. This PR introduces a lightweight timezone-aware shift annotator that canonicalizes shift boundaries to the viewer's timezone, annotates DST-awareness, and exposes a compact rotations export (CSV and ICS) to allow sharing concise schedules with external calendar systems.

What this PR does: Implements a tz-aware rule engine in the slo-toolkit library that: 1) attaches normalized start/end timestamps with timezone metadata; 2) computes human-friendly labels (local time with DST flag) and a compact one-line summary for each shift; 3) exposes a new CLI command `rotations export --compact --tz <zone>` that writes either CSV or ICS entries optimized for large rotation sets. The change is feature-gated behind `tzShiftAnnotator` and default-off for existing customers.

Technical details: The annotator lives at src/annotators/tz_shift_annotator.py and uses python-dateutil + zoneinfo fallback for older environments. It avoids modifying canonical rotation records; instead it emits decorated views used by the exporter, pager templates, and the web preview. Exporter serializes minimal ICS VEVENTs (no alarms) to reduce size and a compact CSV with columns [rotation_id, local_date, start_local, end_local, tz, brief_label]. The CLI and library include explicit DST regression tests.

Compatibility and safety: No data migrations. Storage layout unchanged; all annotated fields are derived at read-time. Feature flag `tzShiftAnnotator` controlled via scripts/feature_toggle.yaml for staged rollout. Unit and integration tests cover canonical fallbacks when zone information is missing.

Testing and CI: Added tests/tests/test_tz_dst.py to validate common DST edge-cases (US, EU, Australia, and Antarctic zones used in CI matrix). Added lightweight e2e that runs the CLI export on a synthetic 200-rotation fixture to validate size and parseability by downstream calendar parsers.

Rollout plan: Merge to main with feature flag off. Enable in a 5% canary (internal infra) for 48 hours, validate telemetry for increases in exported size and error rates, then ramp to 100% region-by-region. If unexpected formatting errors occur, gate off and patch.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of annotator and exporter
- [x] Unit tests for DST and timezone edge cases
- [x] CLI help and docs (docs/rotations.md)
- [x] Feature-flag gating and toggle script
- [x] Telemetry hooks for export failures

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids adding calendar alarms or mutating customer calendars. Exported ICS entries are meant to be imported as read-only references. Related work: ENG-1975 (oncall UX improvements), PM-845 (rotation export product request).

review_comments: Marco Liu (2026-02-12): Nice incremental design. Please ensure the annotator never writes to the DB and confirm fallback semantics when rotation records lack a tz field.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-12): Reply: annotator is read-only by design; added explicit fallback to UTC in code and tests to document behavior.

Sofia Romero (2026-02-13): Request changes: add tests for DST gaps (spring forward) where local times are skipped and for ambiguous times (fall back). Also we should cap ICS export size per-file to avoid giant calendar blobs.
Aisha Patel (2026-02-14): Reply: added tests for gap/ambiguous cases and chunking for ICS exports (max 500 events/file). Noted in docs.
merge_details: Squash merge by Aisha Patel after approvals from Marco and Sofia. No conflicts. Feature flagged off by default.
notes_for_operators: Feature flag tzShiftAnnotator controlled in scripts/feature_toggle.yaml. To enable for a customer namespace, flip flag and monitor slo_toolkit.exports.tz_failures metric. Rolling back is safe - feature is read-only and reversible.
observability_changes: Added telemetry counter slo_toolkit.exports.tz_failures and histogram slo_toolkit.exports.compact_size_bytes; wired into existing dashboards under SLO Toolkit -> Exports.
docs_added: docs/rotations.md describes the export formats, CLI examples, feature flag, and DST notes.
security_considerations: No new privileged APIs. ICS files intentionally omit alarms and tokens. CSV output sanitized to avoid newline injection; tests included.
